package_info.package_manager: custom firmware (Linux-based, not a standard package manager)
package_info.package_versions: unspecified; affected versions use Linux kernel EOL 2016 and packages up to 23 years old
package_info.why_malicious: The firmware is not intentionally malicious, but it is built on severely outdated and unsupported components, including Linux kernels and userland packages that have reached end-of-life (EOL) as early as 2016 and up to 23 years ago. This exposes users to hundreds of known, unpatched critical vulnerabilities, creating a persistent and severe risk of compromise. The lack of transparency, absence of a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), and use of unsupported software make it impossible to assess or mitigate risk, which is a critical security concern.

behavioral_signatures: Firmware images embedding Linux kernel versions that reached end-of-life (EOL) before 2017.
Bundling of userland software packages with known critical vulnerabilities, some released over 10 years ago.
Absence of a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) or any transparency regarding component versions and patch status.
file_indicators: Firmware images containing Linux kernel binaries with version strings indicating EOL status (e.g., kernel version 2.6.x, 3.x, or 4.x with EOL before 2017).
Presence of userland binaries or libraries (e.g., OpenSSL, BusyBox, glibc) with build or release dates more than 10 years old.
Lack of SBOM or manifest files listing component versions.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Extract and analyze firmware images to identify embedded Linux kernel and userland package versions. Flag any firmware using kernels or packages that are end-of-life or have known critical vulnerabilities. Require and review SBOMs for all firmware releases to ensure transparency of included components. Use automated vulnerability scanners to enumerate and assess the risk of all embedded software. Alert on firmware images lacking SBOMs or containing components with EOL status or unpatched CVEs.
